title: Existence of affine Hom generator extension
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open, A = Gamma(Y,U), and T a functor equipped with an equality to the associated-sheaf functor followed by restriction along U.isoSpec [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Let e:T(A) -> O_U be an isomorphism equipped with a heterogeneous equality to tildeSelf followed by restrictUnitIso [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module]. For arbitrary A-modules M,N, there exists c:T(Hom_A(M,N))->internalHom(T(M),T(N)) [def-pur-sheaf-hom] such that for every A-linear h:M->N the composite e inverse, then T(a |-> a*h), then c equals the unit-to-internal-Hom morphism representing T(h) under unitHomEquiv and homObjSectionsEquiv. No uniqueness is asserted.

proof.text: Substitute the equation fixing T. Compose the tilde/global-sections adjunction with restriction along the affine chart. The resulting left adjoint T is additive, as it preserves colimits. The assignment alpha(h) = e.hom followed by the unit-to-internal-Hom section representing T(h) is additive; this is checked componentwise using the two section equivalences.

Prove scalar compatibility of tilde on all opens by evaluating sections at prime ideals and inducting on localized-module fractions. Transport the resulting identity through the chart ring isomorphisms. Naturality of appIso shows that its scalar sections restrict compatibly. Evaluating internal-Hom sections on an over-object and using linearity of e proves alpha(r*h) = T(a |-> a*r) followed by alpha(h). The normalized equation specifying e is unnecessary for this step: any linear rank-one isomorphism works.

Let S be the right adjoint of T. Take the adjunct A -> S(internalHom) of alpha(h) and evaluate it at one. Additivity of the adjunction equivalence and its naturality under multiplication by r make these values an A-linear map Hom_A(M,N) -> S(internalHom). Let c be its adjoint. Adjunction naturality under a |-> a*h, followed by extensionality of linear maps out of A, proves T(a |-> a*h) followed by c = alpha(h). Precompose with e.inv and cancel e.inv followed by e.hom to obtain the stated normalization. No finite presentation or quasi-coherence of internal Hom is used, and zero rings and zero modules require no special case.

based_on.place: Lemma 26.7.1 (lemma-compare-constructions), mapping property; Tag 01HV (4)-(7), localization and functoriality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affineHom_generator_extension {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.affineOpens)
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U.1)) :
    ∀ (T : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U.1) ⥤ U.1.toScheme.Modules)
      (e : T.obj (ModuleCat.of Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(Y, U.1)) ≅
        SheafOfModules.unit U.1.toScheme.ringCatSheaf),
      T = tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom →
      HEq e ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom).mapIso tildeSelf ≪≫
        Scheme.Modules.restrictUnitIso U.2.isoSpec.hom) →
    ∃ c : T.obj (ModuleCat.of Γ(Y, U.1) (M ⟶ N)) ⟶
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf) (T.obj M) (T.obj N),
      ∀ h : M ⟶ N,
        (e.inv ≫ T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom
          (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton Γ(Y, U.1) (ModuleCat.of Γ(Y, U.1) (M ⟶ N)) h))) ≫ c =
          (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
            (T.obj M) (T.obj N)).unitHomEquiv.symm
              ((SheafOfModules.homObjSectionsEquiv (T.obj M) (T.obj N)).symm (T.map h))
